# Squatch Docs

Documentation built with SiteSquatch. This starter has a sidebar, a table of contents on each page, previous and next links, notes and tabs, highlighted code, a link checker and a schema for front matter.

[Read the docs](https://example.com/docs/index.md)

</div>

---
url: https://example.com/docs/
---

# Introduction

Welcome! This is a documentation site built with [SiteSquatch](https://github.com/reverentgeek/sitesquatch). It's yours to change: every file is in this folder, and there's no theme to fight.

## Where things live

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `src/docs/` | The pages, in Markdown. A folder is a section of the URL. |
| `src/_data/nav.yml` | The sidebar, which also gives each page its breadcrumbs and previous and next links. |
| `src/_data/site.json` | The site's name and description. |
| `src/_includes/` | The layouts (`base.edge`, `doc.edge`), and the templates behind headings, tabs and details. |
| `src/assets/` | The stylesheet (its colors are custom properties at the top), and a small script for tabs, search, copying a heading's link and the light and dark switch. |
| `ssqch.config.js` | The config: highlighting, the link checker, the schema for front matter. |

## Add a page

1. Create `src/docs/guides/my-page.md` with a `title` in its front matter.
2. List it in `src/_data/nav.yml`.

That's it. Run `ssqch serve` and it's at `/docs/guides/my-page/`.

:::tip[Owl's field guide]
Owl reads the sidebar from the top: install first, then [Writing pages](https://example.com/docs/guides/writing/index.md), whose source uses every kind of block once, so it doubles as a cheat sheet.
:::

Next: [install ssqch](https://example.com/docs/install/index.md), or see [what a page can do](https://example.com/docs/guides/writing/index.md).

---
url: https://example.com/docs/guides/deploying/

# Deploying

`ssqch build` writes plain files to `dist/`. Any static host can serve them.

## Netlify

```toml
# netlify.toml
[build]
  publish = "dist"
  command = "npx ssqch build"

[build.environment]
  NODE_VERSION = "24"
```

With `ssqch` in the site's `devDependencies` (see [Installation](https://example.com/docs/install/index.md)), Netlify installs it at the version in the lockfile, so a build next year uses the ssqch you tested with. `NODE_VERSION` can be any Node from 22.18 on.

## GitHub Pages

A project site is served under its repository's name, like `https://you.github.io/repo/`. Set that path in `ssqch.config.js`, and leave the links in your pages as they are:

```js
export default defineConfig({
  base: "/repo/",
});
```

Then build it in a workflow with `actions/setup-node`, and deploy `dist/` with GitHub's own Pages actions (in the repository's settings, set Pages' source to "GitHub Actions"):

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pages.yml
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: github-pages
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # every commit, for each page's "Last updated" date
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx ssqch build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: dist
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

## Check before you publish

Build the site before and after a big change, and compare the two:

```sh
npx ssqch build --output dist-before
# ...make the change...
npx ssqch build
npx ssqch diff dist-before dist
```

It lists the pages that were added, removed and changed, and ignores what doesn't matter.

:::note[Beaver's build notes]
Beaver keeps `dist-before/` until the diff shows only what she meant to change. A dam is easier to fix before the water arrives.
:::

# Writing pages

Pages are Markdown, with GitHub's extensions and a few of ssqch's own. This page uses each of them once, so its source is a cheat sheet.

## Notes

:::note
A `:::note` block. There are `:::tip`, `:::warning` and `:::caution` too.
:::

:::warning[Check twice]
Give a block a title in brackets.
:::

> [!TIP]
> **Deer's shortcut:** GitHub's alert syntax works as well, which keeps a README readable in both places.

:::details How do these work?
Each `:::name` block renders through `src/_includes/containers/name.edge` if there is one (like this one, `details.edge`), or as a `<div class="name">`.
:::

## Tabs

::::tabs
:::tab npm
```sh
npm install pinecone
```
:::
:::tab pnpm
```sh
pnpm add pinecone
```
:::
::::

Without JavaScript, tabs are labeled sections, one after another. With it, picking a tab picks it in every group on the site that has one with that name.

## Code

Fences are highlighted while the site builds. Mark lines with braces:

```js {2}
export function trail(name) {
  return `/trails/${name}/`;
}
```

## Tables, tasks and footnotes

| Syntax | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `- [x] done` | A checked box |
| `[^1]` | A footnote[^1] |

- [x] Write the docs
- [ ] Spot a Squatch

## Data in a page

Front matter and the files in `src/_data/` are available in every page: this site is called Squatch Docs.

[^1]: Footnotes collect at the end of the page.

# Installation

`ssqch` runs on [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 22.18 or newer, and comes from npm. Install it in the site as a dev dependency, so the lockfile pins the version:

::::tabs
:::tab npm
```sh
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev ssqch
```
:::
:::tab pnpm
```sh
pnpm init
pnpm add -D ssqch
```
:::
::::

Then run it with `npx ssqch` (or `pnpm ssqch`), or by name in a `package.json` script: `"build": "ssqch build"`. To have `ssqch` on your `PATH` for every site, `npm install --global ssqch` or `brew install reverentgeek/tap/ssqch`.

## Run the site

```sh
npx ssqch serve
```

Open <http://localhost:8080>. Pages rebuild and the browser reloads as you save, and that includes `ssqch.config.js`.

## Build it

```sh
npx ssqch build
```

The site is in `dist/`, ready for any static host. A broken link or a page without a `title` stops the build and says where.

:::tip
`npx ssqch build` also builds a search index with [Pagefind](https://pagefind.app) and adds a search button to the header (or press Ctrl+K, or Cmd+K on a Mac). Pagefind is a program of its own, which `npx` fetches the first time, at the version `ssqch.config.js` pins; `SEARCH=0 npx ssqch build` skips it, for a build with no network. `npx ssqch serve` builds without it, so to try search, build and serve that build: `npx ssqch build`, then `npx ssqch serve --built`.
:::
